card: Escapes backslashes in the Tor control AUTHENTICATE command when using HASHEDPASSWORD authentication. Currently, Bitcoin Core only escapes quotation marks, which causes Tor's control-spec parser to interpret backslashes in -torpassword as escape sequences, altering the password or corrupting the command. The author confirmed that a password containing backslashes fails authentication against Tor 0.4.9.12 on master and succeeds with this patch.
evidence: Author verified against Tor 0.4.9.12: "with HashedControlPassword set for pa\ss"word\: on master bitcoind logs 'tor: Authentication failed', with this change authentication succeeds and ADD_ONION creates the onion service" (PR description).
problem: When authenticating to the Tor control port with `HASHEDPASSWORD`, Bitcoin Core sends the password inside a quoted string but only escapes double quotes. Tor interprets backslashes as escape characters, so passwords containing backslashes are altered or malform the command syntax, causing authentication to fail and preventing onion service creation.

risk.why: A mistake would only prevent nodes configured with Tor control passwords from successfully authenticating to the Tor control port.

summary: Escapes backslashes in addition to quotation marks when transmitting `-torpassword` in the Tor control port `AUTHENTICATE` command under `HASHEDPASSWORD` authentication. Also adds a functional test case using a mock Tor control server.
